  • Work as a peer to hiring managers and leadership: run intakes that sharpen unclear requirements, research and advise when a profile isn't feasible, calibrate on candidates, and hold the process to a standard when timelines get tight.

  • Develop sourcing strategies for talent that rarely applies; from passive outreach, Boolean, referrals, networking, and competitive intelligence across travel tech, marketplaces, and B2B SaaS.

  • Maintain pipelines for critical and recurring roles, so we're not starting from zero each time a requisition opens.

  • Coach hiring managers on interviewing and keep our assessment consistent as teams grow.

  • Use hiring data, funnel conversion, time-to-hire, and source effectiveness to change how we hire, not just to report on it.

  • Manage delivery and efficiency by keeping the ATS accurate, managing candidate experience, and project managing several pipelines.

  • Participate on a series of projects and initiatives that drive talent intelligence without compromising your core role.

Workplace: Berlin & Hybrid
We are looking for this role to be based at our headquarters in Berlin. Despite our Global footprint, our HQ office is in Berlin, and the team often meets in the office.


Who you are:

  • You want to grow, learn and be a true Business Talent Partner to an exciting business and industry

  • You have a high level of integrity and intellectual humility; it is about putting the right attitude in

  • You are driven, ambitious and willing to put in the work necessary to be successful

  • Ideally, you bring some experience in Talent Partnership, finding the right talent for an organisation and the ability to work at scale

Mobileye is looking for a passionate Systems Software Developer to join the Operating System Team in the EyeQ Platform Software Group. While many work on Linux, we work in Linux. Our team is responsible for the core OS DNA of the EyeQ computer vision SoC, defining how the system starts, is composed, and manages its lifecycle in a high-performance automotive environment.

We are looking for an experienced systems engineer to join our Core Distribution team. The center of this role is the Linux userspace and the distribution itself: boot and service bring-up, root filesystem composition, and the integration of external SDK into that platform. You will also build Python-based deployment tooling so the OS and SDK stack can be provisioned reproducibly - infrastructure and tool development in service of the OS.


What will your job look like:
  • Architect and develop Linux userspace and service bring-up so the distribution boots into a consistent, operational platform under embedded constraints. 
  • Enable and integrate an SDK into the OS image - drivers, libraries, runtimes, and filesystem layout as first-class distribution components.
  • Own distribution composition, including packages, sysroots, and image features that make the SDK and core OS a maintainable, versioned platform.
  • Develop Python-based deployment tooling to provision targets with a reproducible OS + SDK environment (image delivery, flashing, and environment setup).
  • Debug at the OS boundary - init/service failures, library and ABI mismatches, missing dependencies, and SDK/runtime issues on the target.
  • Perform root cause analysis on system-level failures in the distribution, from boot and userspace bring-up through a fully operational stack.
  • Collaborate on board bring-up, tailoring the distribution and SDK integration to new EyeQ generations and related target hardware.

    • All you need is:
  • Outstanding graduate in Computer Science or similar field.  
  • 5+ years of experience in Embedded Linux development, with a focus on systems software, userspace, or distribution work.
  • Strong C/C++ skills and a solid understanding of POSIX APIs, libraries, and how userspace talks to the kernel.
  • Deep knowledge of Linux Internals, specifically the boot process (Bootloaders, Kernel hand-off, Init systems) and root filesystem layout.
  • Hands-on experience with Embedded Linux Distributions (e.g., custom Yocto recipes, Buildroot, or Linux-from-scratch).
  • Experience enabling vendor SDKs or BSP stacks on Linux — integrating third-party drivers, runtimes, and userspace components into a custom image.
  • Proficiency in debugging tools like GDB, Valgrind, strace, and perf.
  • Experience with Python for infrastructure and tool development — deployment, packaging, and environment setup.

    • Nice to have:
  • Background in Automotive Software.
  • Experience with GPU/accelerator compute stacks (driver + userspace runtime, inference/compute libraries, cross-sysroot workflows).
  • Familiarity with reading hardware schematics and reasoning about basic hardware interfaces and signal.

Help Build Europe's Hypersonic Capability
 
At Hypersonica, we’re redefining what’s possible in European defence technology. We exist to deliver speed, resilience, and technological independence at a pace that sets a new standard. We are a small, elite team working on problems that matter, and solving them fast.
 
By joining Hypersonica, you’re not stepping into a predefined role. You’re joining a talent dense environment where every individual shapes the direction of the company. Our philosophy is to hire a small number of exceptional people with broad, deep technical capability, strong judgement, and the ability to operate autonomously.
 
We hire for talent, not rigid boxes. This role represents a business need, but the way it evolves will be shaped by the individual. If you’ve achieved what others said was impossible, or you bring a unique combination of skills that doesn’t fit a traditional mould, we want to hear from you. The work you do here directly contributes to Europe’s technological independence.

Getting complex hardware through development and into flight is one challenge. Building the industrial capability to deliver it repeatedly, at the required quality and rate, is another. We’re looking for a Director of Industrialisation to lead that work in Germany.

You’ll take a greenfield manufacturing site from an empty floor to sustained series production. You’ll shape the facility, decide what we build in-house, bring in the equipment and people, and lead the ramp until the operation can deliver reliably. Your job starts while the product is still taking shape, when the right manufacturing decision can save months of work later.

We’re looking for someone who’s done this before and wants to build again. You’ll work directly with the founders and with Engineering, Programmes, Quality, Supply Chain and Operations. You’ll be close enough to the floor to see where the plan is breaking down, and senior enough to make the decisions that fix it.


What you’ll do

  • Own the industrialisation plan. Translate programme demand into a plan for capacity, capital investment, people and suppliers. Set milestones from facility readiness through pilot builds and production ramp, and make the trade-offs visible when timelines or assumptions change.

  • Build and commission the operation. Define what the site needs to support, shape the layout and material flow, and lead equipment selection, installation and commissioning. Plan how the operation will expand as demand grows.

  • Bring manufacturing into product decisions early. Work with Engineering to make the hardware practical to build, inspect and test. Bring evidence from the floor into design reviews, and agree how changes will be introduced as the design matures.

  • Decide what to make and what to buy. Work with Supply Chain to establish which capabilities we need to own, where specialist suppliers make sense, and how we qualify and scale those suppliers alongside our own production.

  • Take pilot builds into repeatable production. Use early builds to expose what will limit output. Resolve bottlenecks, improve yield and build consistency, and demonstrate that the operation can sustain its target rate across successive builds.

  • Build the team and the way it works. Hire the people who will establish the operation. Give them clear ownership, develop leaders on the floor, and put in place the training and routines that let the team solve problems as production grows.

  • Own manufacturing readiness. Define the evidence needed before increasing the rate, from process capability and trained operators to supplier readiness, inspection and traceability. Work with Quality and Safety to build those requirements into everyday work.

  • Make the hard calls. Decide where automation earns its place, where a simpler process gets us there sooner, and where to commit capital before all the answers are in. Give leadership a clear view of what’s on track, what’s at risk and what decision is needed.


    • Who you are

  • You’ve personally led a greenfield site or a major production operation built from scratch, through commissioning and into sustained series or volume production. You can tell us what existed on day one, what you owned and what the operation was delivering once it ramped.

  • You’ve industrialised complex hardware while the design was still evolving. You know how to keep engineering and manufacturing moving together when a design change affects tooling, suppliers, inspection or the delivery plan.

  • You’ve made consequential capital, capacity and staffing decisions. You can explain what you committed to early, what you deliberately kept flexible and how those choices played out.

  • You’ve lived through a difficult ramp. You can talk us through a target you missed, how you found the real constraint, what you changed and what happened to output, yield, cost or delivery as a result.

  • You’ve built and led teams across disciplines. You can earn the trust of operators, technicians and engineers, challenge a design decision with evidence, and explain a manufacturing trade-off to the founders in plain language.

  • You know how to build at pace in a demanding hardware environment. You put the controls that matter in place early, and keep decisions close to the people doing the work.

  • You’re motivated by the opportunity to build industrial capability for European defence, and you want to be on site with the team doing it.


    • Where you might have done it
    You might have launched a new factory in automotive, built a production operation at a hardware startup, or taken an aerospace or advanced manufacturing product from low-rate builds to series production.
     
    You could have done it inside a larger company if you had the mandate to build the operation and were personally accountable for the ramp.The common thread is the build itself. We want to hear about the operation you created, how quickly you brought it online, the rate it sustained and the decisions you made when the original plan met reality.

    What we offer

  • Genuine ownership of the industrialisation of one of Europe’s most ambitious defence engineering programmes, from an empty site to sustained series production.

  • The chance to join early enough that your decisions will shape the factory, the team and how Hypersonica manufactures for years to come.

  • Direct access to the founders and the factory floor, with short decision paths and the authority to act when you see a better way to build.

  • Daily collaboration with exceptional people across Engineering, Manufacturing, Quality, Supply Chain, Test and Programmes. You’ll have a seat at the table while the product is still taking shape.

  • The freedom to challenge convention and build from first principles, from what we make in-house to where automation earns its place.

  • The resources and ambition to build a production operation at a pace that would be hard to match in a traditional aerospace organisation.

  • The chance to see your decisions through, from the first factory layout on a whiteboard to hardware coming off a line that delivers reliably, shift after shift.

    • At Hypersonica, every hire raises the bar. We are deliberately small, intensely capable, and deeply mission-driven. If this role feels like a strong fit, or if you believe you bring something exceptional that goes beyond the description, we encourage you to apply.
     
    Hypersonica is an equal-opportunity employer and assesses candidates solely on merit, capability, and potential.
     
    You can apply directly to this role or reach out to Nathan Sweeney, Head of Talent. We review every application and aim to respond to all candidates within two weeks, whether the answer is yes or no.

Fitness is the one industry where customers actually enjoy using the product. Help us tell that story well. At Sport Alliance, we're looking for someone who can bring clarity to our product portfolio and help us connect the right products with the right customers across different markets.

Every one of our products needs a clear reason to exist, a clear customer and a clear story. You’ll work alongside Product from the earliest sizing and segmentation conversations through to launch and adoption, so what we build is what the market wants and what Sales can sell.

As our Senior Product Marketing Manager, you'll shape product positioning, packaging, and go-to-market strategies, turning complex offerings into clear value propositions that Sales can confidently bring to customers. 


Your position in our team

  • Tell one clear story per product. Own product positioning and messaging across our brands, creating clear, differentiated value propositions tailored to customer segments and markets.

  • Help decide what gets built, and why. Build market sizing and segmentation, and work with product so what we build meets customer needs and drives growth.

  • Shape packaging. Shape product packaging, working closely with Product, Pricing and Finance.

  • Launch things properly. Own go-to-market for key launches, from sizing and planning through to enablement. Join early, before the build, so the commercial view shapes the product from day one. Build a repeatable launch process that makes every launch smoother than the last.

  • Show what worked. Track adoption and conversion of new features and modules against the uplift we forecast. Where we hit it, find ways to do more. Where we didn't, learn why and feed it back into strategy. Your measures: product attachment, expansion MRR, win rate by segment and average deal value by product.

  • Stay close to customers and competitors. Talk to customers directly, run buyer research and win/loss, and own our ICPs. Build competitive intelligence as a living asset, with an AI agent doing the heavy lifting.

  • Equip Sales to win. Own the sales-facing narrative and build the tools: pitch narratives, battlecards, ROI calculators, case studies. Then see which ones get used and which ones move deals. Enable the sales team to tell the right story, and track whether they get used.

  • Build it, don't brief it. Use AI to speed up research and prototype pages, calculators and demos yourself. Hand the best ones to the agency or web team to scale.


    • Your profile

  • 6+ years of experience in Product Marketing, Product Management or a commercially focused product role within B2B SaaS.

  • Ability to build and communicate strong commercial value cases or ROI models.

  • A hands-on approach to creating assets such as prototypes, pages and calculators: you build, test and improve rather than simply brief others.

We built ClearBank on the belief that banking infrastructure would no longer slow down progress. Instead, it would be a catalyst that unlocks the potential to innovate. It would adapt to different needs so a new era in financial services could begin. We’re here to challenge the status quo in banking, are you?

We all know that transforming banking forever is not an easy mission, but we’re more than ready to rise to that challenge. We all do it every day; navigating new, unexpected and sometimes even daunting challenges. But we believe in ourselves and trust we can do it. Want to innovate? Go for it. Push for a better way? You Can. If you think you have it in you, this is Where You Can.

About Us

ClearBank is a technology‑enabled, fully regulated bank providing cloud‑based banking and payments infrastructure to financial institutions. We operate at scale in a highly regulated environment, where trust, resilience and security are critical.

Our engineering organisation is focused on enabling frequent, reliable change while maintaining strong controls. We believe quality is not a gate at the end of delivery, but something designed in from the very start.

Role Purpose

This is a senior leadership role accountable for the strategy, design, build, operation and ongoing resilience of ClearBank’s payments and cards platforms.

The VP of Payments & Cards will lead multiple engineering teams responsible for real-time, scheme-connected payments and cards systems across the UK, Europe, and future international markets. This requires deep experience working close to the infrastructure that moves money. Ideally, this will include direct integration with major payment schemes or rails, such as FPS, Bacs or CHAPS in the UK, SEPA payment schemes in Europe, or ACH and Fedwire in the US. We will also consider experience gained through payment infrastructure providers or connectivity platforms provided it includes sufficient technical depth in payment processing, scheme connectivity and the operation of highly available, regulated payments infrastructure. The role will define platform strategy, engineering standards, tooling and ways of working, while embedding a shift-left quality mindset across delivery. Success means delivering highly resilient, highly available, secure, scalable and compliant platforms that enable frequent, reliable change in a regulated banking environment.

Key Responsibilities

  • Own the strategy, design, build and run of real-time payments and cards platforms across the UK, Europe, the US and future international markets, including direct scheme connectivity and integrations with third-party payment infrastructure providers.

  • Lead the delivery and operation of digital wallet capabilities, including Apple Pay and Google Pay implementations.

  • Set the technical direction for payments and cards platforms, ensuring architectural choices support resilience, availability, scalability, performance, security and cost efficiency.

  • Own the budget for the Payments and Cards engineering teams, ensuring effective investment in people, tooling and platforms.

  • Build, lead and develop high-performing engineering teams, creating clear accountability, strong delivery discipline and a culture of engineering excellence.

  • Ensure platforms are designed and operated to meet the following outcomes:

  • Highly resilient — supporting local and cross-region disaster recovery requirements.

  • Highly available — targeting 99.999% aggregate internal availability where appropriate.

  • Highly scalable — supporting aggressive growth targets and future business volumes.

  • Performant — meeting scheme performance requirements and exceeding client expectations on latency.

  • Cost optimised — balancing client value, operational efficiency and ClearBank’s cost base.

  • Establish scalable engineering quality standards, practices and governance across the payments and cards domain.

  • Embed quality, observability, operational readiness and control requirements into delivery practices and CI/CD pipelines.

  • Drive engineering productivity through AI-assisted and increasingly agentic software engineering, including the effective use of AI coding tools and multi-agent approaches across development, testing and engineering workflows, with appropriate risk, security and regulatory guardrails.

  • Partner closely with the CTO, engineering leaders, product, risk, compliance and operations teams to ensure delivery decisions balance pace, quality and control.

  • Ensure software development and platform operations meet regulatory, audit, resilience and compliance expectations.

Skills & Experience

  • Senior engineering leadership experience in payments, cards or highly regulated financial technology environments.

  • Proven experience establishing, scaling and operating engineering teams, standards and practices.

  • Direct experience integrating with, building against or operating connectivity to payment schemes or rails. Relevant examples include Faster Payments, Bacs or CHAPS in the UK; SEPA payment schemes and associated euro payment infrastructure in Europe; ACH or Fedwire in the US; or card networks and associated issuing or acquiring infrastructure. Alternatively, substantial experience delivering payment connectivity through a provider such as Form3 or an equivalent platform, with demonstrable technical depth in how payments are processed, routed and operated.

  • Experience delivering or operating digital wallet capabilities, such as Apple Pay and Google Pay.

  • Strong understanding of real-time, high-availability, high-throughput distributed systems.

  • Strong background working in regulated environments, with practical experience of audit, compliance, operational resilience and control frameworks.

  • Deep understanding of shift-left quality, test automation, modern quality engineering and secure software development practices.

  • Experience using modern AI-enabled engineering tooling and a strong understanding of how agentic or multi-agent approaches can improve software development, testing and engineering delivery in a controlled and responsible way.

  • Strong security mindset, with an appreciation of evolving threats, mitigations and secure platform design.

  • Demonstrated ability to influence across multiple teams and senior stakeholders, including where direct line management is not present.

  • Excellent collaboration and communication skills, with the ability to work effectively with engineering, product, risk, compliance and executive stakeholders.

  • Sound judgement in balancing delivery pace, customer outcomes, regulatory expectations, operational risk and engineering quality.

A little bit more about us! 

ClearBank is Where You Can belong: 

At ClearBank we think about Diversity, Equity and Inclusion (DE&I) a lot. Not because we think we should. But because we know we should – how else can we build a happy workforce and be successful as a business. We’re committed to making sure our teams reflect society. And we put energy and effort into making this a place where everyone feels at home, where they’re given the trust and encouragement to do their very best work. Here are some of the things we’re most proud of: 

  • 42% of our senior management roles are held by women 

  • Our enhanced family leave policies

  • Launching our partnership with Code First Girls 

  • Increasing awareness of neurodiversity in the workplace through our partnership with the Inclusive Group 

Our hiring process and what you can expect:

Application: a member of our talent acquisition team will review your application against the key requirements for the role and let you know within two weeks whether you’re moving forward to the next stage; 

Screening: You’ll spend 30-45 minutes speaking to one of our recruiters learning more about the role and ClearBank, and we’ll get it know more about you, your experience and how your skills align with the role (this will be via phone or Teams video call). You can expect to hear back from us within seven days following this meeting (if things are taking longer than expected, we’ll let you know that too); 

First Interview: You’ll spend one hour with a member of our hiring team focusing on your skills, competencies and your ways of working at the same time we’ll give you time to ask more questions about the role, the team and learn more about the ClearBank culture. This will be via Teams.  

Second Interview: This will be a competency-based interview with one or more members of our team.

Final Stage: You will have a final meeting with the Head of Department. This will be around 45-60 minutes.  

Offer: Congratulations! Get ready to transform banking forever! 

 

Our commitment to you as a candidate: 

We will always try our best to get back to you within seven days of your interview whether you’ve been successful or not and provide you with feedback. Sometimes things take a little longer, so we may not have a decision to share but we will get it touch to let you know we need a little more time.  

We’re unable to provide specific individual feedback at the application or screening stage but know that your application was reviewed and considered carefully.  

We wish you the best of luck with your application and maybe we’ll be celebrating your new role at ClearBank soon!  

Equal Opportunities

ClearBank is committed to ensuring equal opportunities throughout every stage of the recruitment process. ClearBank recognises that diversity is vital to the long-term success of the business in the communities and markets in which it operates. ClearBank is also a firm believer that an inclusive culture fosters greater employee engagement and collaboration. 

ClearBank strives for diversity and inclusion of all forms, including (but not limited to): gender, age, educational and professional background, disability, gender reassignment, marital or civil partner status, pregnancy or maternity, race, colour, nationality, ethnic or national origin, religion or belief and sexual orientation. 

As part of the Company’s commitment to equal employment opportunity, we provide reasonable adjustments, to candidates during the recruitment process, including to individuals with disabilities. We want to create a safe space that welcomes everyone so please let us know how we can accommodate you. In case you have any accessibility requirements you can share that with our Talent Acquisition team prior to your interview stage, if applicable. 

The legal bit

By submitting your CV to ClearBank Limited you are providing your consent for us to use the information you provide for recruitment purposes. For more information on how we manage your data go and check out our Candidate Privacy Notice on the ClearBank website to see how we process, manage and look after your data. You are also allowing us to communicate with you by email and telephone for recruitment purposes.

ABOUT BEAMERY

With the rapid expansion of AI and automation, the future of work has never been more challenging for organizations. Beamery’s unique jobs, skills and tasks data platform helps organizations navigate these challenges and make more informed decisions across Talent Lifecycle Management. Our solutions power recruitment, mobility, upskilling, diversity, work architecture and workforce planning for some of the world’s most forward-thinking companies.

We believe that where you work is much more than just a job. Millions of people are being left behind every day in their careers, and we’re on a mission to fix this by creating equal access to meaningful work, skills and careers for all.

We are an equal opportunity employer committed to building a representative Beamery, creating an equitable, inclusive and engaging environment for our people.

So, what are you waiting for? Join us and help us transform the future of work once and for all.

What’s ahead — and why it’s an exciting time to join the team: 

Building agentic AI with advanced orchestration (multi-agent workflows, tool use, evaluation loops) that turns complex talent data into decisions.

  • Training and fine-tuning our own models on unique data about jobs, skills and tasks, and benchmarking them against the best in our market.

  • Joining an award-winning AI team (ACM RecSys Challenge 2026) that turns new ideas into innovative solutions with scientific rigour.

  • Sharing our work and learning from industry peers through challenges, conferences and publications.

But it’s not all about creating high-quality products, we also very much value the company culture we have worked hard to create; built on trust, empathy & honesty ensuring our workforce is able to bring their full selves to work.

About the opportunity at Beamery

We are looking for an experienced Senior Product Manager to own Beamery's Data Foundry end to end. The Data Foundry is our proprietary data platform, powering existing and emerging product lines including our Talent CRM and Workforce Suite. Through this, we provide data-as-a-service to customers through channels such as MCP/API. This is an emerging commercial channel. Its core capabilities span the data models, taxonomies and integrations that underpin talent and workforce decisions across our platform.

The Senior Product Manager, Data Foundry will treat data both as infrastructure embedded within our products and as a product that customers buy in its own right. Beyond internal embedding and direct commercial sales, the platform is open — customers and partners can build on top of it through MCP and API access. You will work with product leadership to set the strategy, agree what the platform provides internally, decide what becomes customer-facing, and define how the platform opens up for customer and partner innovation.

You will work at the centre of the platform, creating a balance between two essential initiatives. On one side, you serve the Talent CRM and Workforce Suite product managers as your customers, agreeing the data contracts they build on. On the other, you partner with the data science, data engineering and integrations engineering leads to turn those needs into delivery.

What you will be doing

Ownership and strategy

  • Own the Data Foundry vision, strategy and roadmap, framing each item as a bet with a clear driver, aligned to overall strategic objectives

  • Ensure alignment of Data Foundry strategy to Beamery's AI strategy, reflecting the shift from providing AI assistants to providing AI access through MCP and API channels.

  • Decide what Data Foundry provides as internal infrastructure and what is packaged and sold as a customer-facing product.

  • Make and defend build versus buy decisions across integrations, analytics, AI and taxonomy capabilities.

Discovery and commercial impact

  • Discover and validate what external customers want from data-as-a-service, and partner with Sales and Customer Success to drive adoption with clear GTM and enablement plans

  • Build the case for Data Foundry as a new commercial channel, defining and proving the standalone commercial model alongside its role as platform foundation, quantify the value it unlocks for specific customers and deals, and measure success against value and usage metrics.

Partnership and delivery

  • Lead your team to deliver solutions our customers can’t imagine working without and that deliver measurable customer and business outcomes

  • Agree and maintain the data contracts with the CRM and Workforce Suite product managers, treating them as internal customers with real commitments.

  • Prioritise across data science, data engineering and integrations engineering, translating tribe needs into a clear and deliverable plan.

Communication & alignment

  • Communicate transparently and create alignment between peers and leadership on priorities, trade offs and progress

  • Manage customer and sales expectations through well managed structured cadences

Data governance and trust

  • Own how workforce data is governed, secured and access-controlled as it is exposed through APIs and MCP, meeting or exceeding enterprise privacy and compliance expectations.

  • Ensure the outputs of Data Foundry's models are measurable and explainable, so customers and internal teams can trust and act on the results.

What we are looking for

  • A product manager with a minimum 6 years experience in complex technical, data or AI products, a significant portion of which should be in enterprise B2B SaaS.

  • Strong grasp of data platforms, APIs and integrations, comfortable making architecture-adjacent decisions while collaborating with and holding priorities with engineering and data science leads.

  • Experience handling sensitive or regulated data, with a clear view of governance, security and privacy.

  • An analytical thinker who uses data to find opportunities, confidently prioritise and measure success, balancing between competing tribe roadmaps and internal customers.

  • Commercially fluent, experience with 0-1 product stages, shaping early product with new go to market motions, able to connect product decisions to revenue, cost and customer ROI.

  • A clear communicator who builds trust across product, data science and engineering, and who is comfortable taking a position and explaining the reasoning.

  • Experienced owning and delivering AI capabilities, with a keen interest in how AI is reshaping the talent and workforce space, and in giving customers trusted, explainable access to their data.

Beamery is for Everybody. Diversity and open expression are fundamental to us. We acknowledge the challenges in our industry and strive to develop an inclusive culture where everybody can contribute. We are dedicated to creating an inclusive environment for everyone, regardless of ethnicity, religion, color, sexual orientation, gender identity, race, national origin, age, disability status, or caregiver status. If, for whatever reason, you need us to make reasonable adjustments and adaptations to our recruitment process, please email Visit our Diversity, Equality and Inclusion page to learn more about progress and commitments.

Chief Medical Officer, UK/I & EMEA

The Role

Lyrebird is reshaping how clinical documentation happens across the NHS and in Ireland, and we’re looking for a Chief Medical Officer to be the senior clinical voice of the business. Reporting to the CEO, you’ll make sure everything we build, deploy and sell is clinically safe, evidence-based and genuinely useful to clinicians and patients. You’ll own our clinical safety and governance framework, including DCB0129 and oversight of the Clinical Safety Officer function. You’ll shape the product roadmap alongside Product and Engineering, build the evidence base that NHS and HSE buyers need, and act as a trusted peer to CCIOs, CMIOs, medical directors and ICB leaders.

This role suits a practising or recently practising doctor who has led at a senior level in the NHS and knows digital health from the inside. You’re comfortable moving between a board presentation, a hazard log and a conversation with engineers in the same afternoon. You’ll enjoy the pace of a high-growth company, but you’ll never trade safety for speed. You believe clinical AI should be held to the same standards as the rest of medicine, and you want to be the person who proves it can be.

About Us

Lyrebird Health is transforming the quality and accessibility of healthcare by automating clinicians’ most time-consuming tasks.

Thousands of clinicians across multiple disciplines use Lyrebird every day in environments where accuracy, safety, and time matter deeply. In the UK, that includes NHS trusts across Cheshire and Merseyside, Alder Hey Children’s, and the South West London Acute Provider Collaborative, one of the largest ambient AI deployments in the country. Everything we build is grounded in earning trust, reducing cognitive load, and delivering meaningful impact at scale.

What you’ll do

  • Lead Lyrebird’s clinical safety management system for the UK and Ireland, ensuring DCB0129 compliance, supporting customers with DCB0160, and providing senior oversight of our Clinical Safety Officers.

  • Bring the clinical voice into the product roadmap, defining UK- and Ireland-specific workflows and leading clinical validation of new models, features and specialty templates before release.

  • Own clinical incident management and chair our clinical governance and safety committee, reporting to the leadership team and board.

  • Advise on the regulatory landscape, including MHRA medical device regulation, NHS England guidance on ambient voice technology, DTAC, and the EU AI Act for Ireland.

  • Design and deliver a clinical evidence strategy, running evaluations and real-world studies with NHS and academic partners, publishing the results, and always reporting limitations honestly.

  • Act as a trusted clinical peer to CCIOs, CMIOs, medical directors and digital leaders across NHS trusts, ICBs and the HSE, and represent Lyrebird at conferences, in the media and in national policy conversations.

  • Bring clinical credibility to the commercial team by leading the clinical, safety and evidence sections of tenders, supporting pilots, and making sure every clinical claim we make stands up.

  • Build and lead a UK and Ireland clinical team, and champion equity, patient safety and inclusive design across languages, accents and patient groups.

What you’ll bring

  • Full GMC registration with a licence to practise, in good standing.

  • Significant senior clinical leadership experience in the NHS, such as Medical Director, Deputy or Associate Medical Director, or Clinical Director.

  • Substantial digital health or clinical informatics leadership, for example as a CCIO, CMIO or senior clinical lead on an EPR or digital transformation programme.

  • In-depth, practical knowledge of DCB0129 and DCB0160, clinical risk management, hazard logs and safety cases, plus a solid grasp of MHRA, DTAC, DSPT and NHS England AI guidance.

  • A track record of designing, leading or publishing clinical evaluations, audits or research.

  • Strong NHS networks and the ability to explain complex clinical, technical and regulatory issues clearly to boards, clinicians, engineers and patients.

Nice to have

  • Accredited Clinical Safety Officer training, and continuing clinical practice alongside the role.

  • Experience in a health tech, MedTech or digital health company, ideally including evaluation of AI or NLP safety and performance.

  • Knowledge of the EU AI Act, EU MDR and the Irish health system, or registration with the Medical Council of Ireland.

  • Membership or fellowship of the Faculty of Clinical Informatics, or a national profile through the Royal Colleges, NHS England or a Health Innovation Network.

  • Familiarity with clinical coding (SNOMED CT, ICD-10, OPCS-4), PRSB standards or the NICE Evidence Standards Framework.

Every minute a clinician spends on documentation is a minute taken from their patients. In this role, you’ll help decide how ambient AI is safely adopted across the NHS and in Ireland, setting the standards that protect patients while giving clinicians time back to focus on care.

We’re building a team that reflects the diversity of the people who benefit from our work. We want Lyrebird to be a place where everyone feels safe, supported, and able to thrive. If you’re from an underrepresented background in tech, we strongly encourage you to apply, even if you don’t meet every requirement.

Who are we?

Smarkets: Predicting the Future of Betting

Smarkets runs one of the world's most sophisticated prediction markets, handling over £29 billion in volume since 2010 and engaging 200,000+ traders globally. We're a technology company that happens to revolutionise betting — from sports to political markets, delivering the sharpest prices and the fairest odds.

We're also growing: we're pursuing licensing with the CFTC to expand into the US market, a significant step in our ambition to become a truly global exchange. Joining now means being part of that next chapter, not just maintaining what's already built.

At the heart of our success are our people. We create a high-performance environment where exceptional talent can thrive, blending deep business experience with a commercial mindset to drive strategic growth.

The Team

Finance makes sure Smarkets has accurate, timely numbers to run the business, satisfy regulators, and stand up to investor scrutiny — across multiple jurisdictions and licences. Two things keep us busy:

  • Reporting & Control — close, statutory accounts, audit, and the controls framework behind a dual UKGC/CFTC regulated business

  • Systems & Transformation — building out reporting on top of our ERP and automating away the manual stuff

A typical week: run a clean close and turn it into a board-ready pack, write a technical paper on a tricky accounting area, ship an automated process and make it audit-ready.

About the Role:

We're looking for a detail-oriented, proactive GL Accountant to take ownership of our core accounting operations and general ledger. In this role, you will play a key part in driving the accuracy of our monthly close, ensuring robust balance sheet integrity, and delivering clear financial reporting for internal and external stakeholders.

This is an operational accounting role where you will own the integrity of the General Ledger end-to-end: keeping ledgers accurate, resolving complex accounting issues, and ensuring audit readiness.

What you will do:

  • Own and maintain the General Ledger (GL), ensuring all financial transactions are accurately recorded and mapped

  • Execute the month-end close (m/e) process efficiently and accurately to tight timelines

  • Perform comprehensive balance sheet and account reconciliations, identifying and resolving any variances

  • Prepare and process VAT, tax returns and payroll

  • Prepare monthly management accounts and deliver insightful variance analysis

  • Assist with cash flow forecasting

  • Support the preparation of year-end financial statements and liaise with external auditors

  • Act as a key liaison to investigate and resolve departmental accounting issues across the business

  • Assist in driving internal control improvements and supporting automation within our AI-driven ERP environment

Role Requirements:

  • Part-qualified or newly qualified ACCA/ACA/CIMA, with a strong foundation in core accounting principles

  • Proven hands-on experience in general ledger management and month-end close processes

  • Strong technical skills in balance sheet reconciliations, journal entries, and financial controls

  • Comfortable working in a fast-moving finance team with high standards of data accuracy

  • Excellent communication and problem-solving skills, capable of resolving cross-departmental queries

  • Experience with ERP systems and process automation tools is a plus

  • Experience in a regulated industry (betting, gaming, financial services, or similar) is a plus

 

Our Values

Our values are at the heart of everything we do - guiding how we work, collaborate, and innovate. They reflect what we expect of ourselves and each other to deliver the best results, while fostering a positive, high-performing environment:

  • Push to Win: We set ambitious goals and relentlessly pursue them, always striving for excellence.

  • Make Others Better: We lift each other up, share knowledge, and celebrate team success over individual achievement.

  • Give a Shit: We care deeply about our work, our users, and the impact we make.

  • Be a Pro: We take ownership, act with integrity, and consistently deliver to a high standard.

  • Bring the Energy: We bring positivity, curiosity, and enthusiasm to everything we do, inspiring those around us.

Culture Fit: These values define how we succeed as a team. If this isn’t you, this may not be the right place. We hire people who thrive in a fast-paced, collaborative, and ambitious environment.

 

Perks & Benefits
We offer a competitive salary and benefits package, alongside a dynamic, collaborative environment where your work truly makes an impact and your voice is heard. Our team is diverse, driven, and ambitious - united by a strong work ethic and a hunger to innovate and win.

Our benefits are designed around Health, Wealth,and Development, supporting you both professionally and personally.

These include:

  • Stock Options: Vest over 4 years - your success is our success.

  • Pension Scheme: Competitive plan via Aviva, with up to 6% matched contributions if you opt in.

  • Health Insurance: Comprehensive coverage to keep you and your family healthy.

  • Enhanced Parental Leave: Enhanced maternity and paternity leave to support you through life’s most important moments.

  • Stay Fuelled: Enjoy fresh, chef-made breakfast and lunch every day, plus a constant supply of fruit, snacks, tea, coffee and soft drinks — because great work starts with great food.

  • Cycle-to-Work Scheme: Support for sustainable commuting and staying active.

  • Learning & Development: £1,000 annual education budget for courses, conferences, books, or training.

  • Holiday: 25 days paid leave + bank holidays, with the option to carry over 5 days.

  • Flexible Working: Hybrid model with 3 days in the office and 2 days from home to fit your lifestyle.

  • Team Energy: Regular socials, hackathons, and events — because collaboration and fun go hand-in-hand.

What happens next​

We aim to have a simple and speedy hiring process, and we want to make sure we're right for you as much as the other way around.

  1. Initial screening — a quick chat with our recruiter about your experience and the role

  2. Experience & mindset interview — a conversation about your background and what drives you

  3. Competency interview — with the hiring manager and team

  4. Lunch & leadership team — lunch with the wider team, plus time with members of our leadership team

Diversity & Inclusion

We’re an equal opportunities employer and celebrate diversity in all its forms. If you need any adjustments during the recruitment process, please let us know — we’re happy to accommodate your needs.

We have offices in San Francisco, New York, Denver, London, Paris, Berlin, Sydney, Mexico City, and remote team members across the US and Europe. We hope that you'll be interested in joining us!

Watershed is on a mission to help companies measure, reduce, and report their emissions. Our go-to-market organization continues to grow, with an emphasis on scale and deepening our presence in EMEA. We're looking for a hands-on operator to run sales operations for the region and build the tools & processes our sellers rely on.

This position is based in our London office 4 days per week.

You will:

  • Support headcount, territory, and quota planning for the region, including account ownership and territory governance

  • Own the EMEA forecasting process: run regular forecast and pipeline reviews, and inspect deals to improve predictability

  • Define and track the metrics that show how our revenue teams are performing, and turn them into clear recommendations for leadership

  • Be the go-to resource for our London office on Salesforce and our revenue tech stack

You have:

  • Direct experience supporting sales teams: you've run a forecast cadence, territory or quota planning, and the reporting behind a revenue number

  • Strong analytical skills, with hands-on experience building models and interpreting sales metrics

At Watershed, we are dedicated to ensuring an inclusive recruitment process. Senior People Partner

Cloudscaler | London | People Team | Reports to the Chief People Officer | £55,000–£75,000

Someone has to own the People initiative that doesn’t fit neatly into anyone’s week and the case nobody else should be handling. That someone is you — not as an escalation point, but as the person who runs the day-to-day of this function.

THE MOMENT

Cloudscaler is 130 people today. We’ll be 170 by the end of this year, and roughly double again in 2027. The People function is being built in real time alongside that growth, rather than inherited from someone who left years ago.

You’ll be the first hire into the People team. For roughly your first year you’ll be the only People professional alongside the CPO, which means running the whole day-to-day of the function: the hardest casework and initiatives, and the operational core that keeps everything moving. A People Partner is planned to join later in 2027, and at that point the operational administration moves to them.

This is also a role built with room to grow. As the team expands beyond that second hire, we expect this role to take on day-to-day operational leadership of the People Partner practice, but that isn’t the shape of it on day one.

WHAT MAKES THIS DIFFERENT

In most People teams, the senior generalist is just a People Partner with a harder case queue. Here, the difference is ownership, not just difficulty.

  • Complex casework: Rather than simply handling harder cases, you’ll own the most complex cases end to end, with no hand back.

  • People initiatives: Rather than contributing to initiatives someone else drives, you’ll own them from design through to embedding.

  • Decision-making: Rather than escalating ambiguity upward, you’ll make the sensible call and document your reasoning.

  • CPO partnership: Rather than acting in a support role to the CPO, you’ll be an operational partner they can confidently delegate to.

To be clear about the level: The CPO still designs the People strategy and the systems architecture. You own how it runs day to day, and you’re trusted to run a whole initiative, not just a case. That is a different job to People Partner, not a bigger version of the same one.

THE ROLE

You’ll sit in the People team reporting to the Chief People Officer. Three strands make up the job:

  • Casework: The employee relations situations with the most complexity or sensitivity land with you, start to finish.

  • Initiatives: When the CPO needs a piece of work owned (a policy rollout, a wellbeing programme, a piece of the reward or benefits agenda), you take it from design through to something that runs.

  • Operations: Until the People Partner joins, you’ll own payroll and benefits administration, onboarding, screening and security clearances, and keeping Rippling accurate.

When the People Partner joins, they’ll report to the CPO. You won’t manage them formally, but you’ll lead their handover, you’ll be the person they come to first, and your judgement will set the standard for how this function operates day to day.

WHERE THE ROLE STARTS AND STOPS

New roles get vague, so here is the boundary as we see it today.

Yours

  • The most complex and sensitive employee relations casework, end to end.

  • Full ownership of People initiatives, from design to embedding.

  • Acting as the CPO’s operational partner on ambiguous or cross-cutting problems.

  • Until the People Partner joins (planned for later in 2027):

    • Payroll and benefits administration, including the monthly payroll cycle in Rippling and Mintago.

    • Pre-onboarding, onboarding and probation.

    • Background screening in Zinc.

    • Security clearance coordination.

    • Rippling data quality, workflows and reporting.

    • Our working groups and committees.

  • Once the People Partner joins:

    • A structured handover of the operational core.

    • Day-to-day guidance for the People Partner.

Shared

  • Ashby, which Talent Acquisition owns. You’ll work in it from offer through to start date on every hire until the People Partner joins, and on senior hires after that.

  • Mentoring and supporting the People Partner on their casework and initiatives, once they join.

Not yours

  • Recruitment delivery, which sits with Talent Acquisition.

  • The design of the People strategy, the operating model and the systems architecture, which sit with the CPO.

  • Formal line management of the People Partner, who will report to the CPO.

THE STACK

  • Rippling: Our single source of truth. Until the People Partner joins you’ll run it day to day, including the monthly payroll cycle, data quality and workflows, and you’ll use its reporting at a level that supports whole initiatives.

  • Zinc: Background screening. You’ll run checks for every new joiner until the People Partner joins, and stay close to the senior and sensitive hires after that.

  • Ashby: Owned by Talent Acquisition. You’ll work in it from offer through to start date on the hires you’re responsible for.

  • Claude: A daily tool here. You’ll use it for casework preparation, drafting policy and communications, and pulling together the analysis behind an initiative.

  • Mintago: Our employee benefits and financial wellbeing platform (pensions, salary sacrifice and financial advice). You’ll administer it and keep enrolment accurate until the People Partner takes it on.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

  • Own the hardest casework. You’ll run our most complex and sensitive employee relations cases end to end, with the CPO there to sense-check rather than take over.

  • Own initiatives, not tasks. You’ll take a People initiative from a rough brief to something that’s running and embedded, rather than handing it back once the interesting part is done.

  • Run the operational core. Until the People Partner joins, you’ll own the monthly payroll cycle in Rippling, benefits administration including Mintago, onboarding, background screening and security clearances. Accurate, on time, and documented as you go.

  • Hand it over well. When the People Partner arrives, you’ll give them a working system and a clear handover, then stay the person they come to first and the judgement others in the function measure themselves against.

  • Partner with senior leaders. You’ll be credible with leaders on the most difficult conversations: complex change, capability, and situations without a clean playbook.

  • Use AI properly. You’ll use Claude daily to take time out of your own week, checking anything that touches a decision about a person and owning the outcome.

  • Improve what you find. You’ll spot the gaps in policy, process or practice before anyone else does, and bring the CPO a considered view on the fix, not just the problem.

WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE AT 12 MONTHS

  • You’re running the most complex ER cases with confidence, and the CPO isn’t being pulled into them.

  • At least one or two People initiatives have gone from a rough brief to something genuinely embedded, owned by you.

  • Payroll, benefits, onboarding and clearances run accurately and on time, and every process is documented well enough to hand over.

  • You’ve helped shape the People Partner hire, so the handover is ready when they land.

  • Senior leaders treat you as a credible operational partner, not an escalation point.

  • You’ve made and documented sensible calls in genuinely ambiguous situations, and they’ve held up.

  • The CPO can hand you an ambiguous problem and trust it gets shaped properly.

WHO WE’RE LOOKING FOR

  • Deep employee relations experience. You’ve run complex disciplinaries, grievances and change situations yourself, and you know exactly when to escalate and when not to. CIPD qualification, or solid progress towards it, is welcome.

  • A track record of owning initiatives. You can point to work you took from a brief to something that actually ran, not just a project you contributed to.

  • Hands-on with the operational detail. You’ve owned or closely supported a payroll cycle, benefits administration and onboarding, and you’re comfortable being accountable for their accuracy while also carrying the senior work.

  • Credible with senior leaders. You can hold your own in a difficult conversation with someone under real pressure and be listened to.

  • Comfortable operating near-autonomously. You don’t need a playbook for everything. You make a sensible call, write it down, and check it with the CPO afterwards.

  • Ready to grow into people leadership. You won’t formally manage anyone at the start, but you’ll induct and guide the People Partner when they join, and you should want to lead a team as the structure catches up.

  • Discreet and organised at volume. Complex casework and live initiatives, often at the same time. You’ll need a system, and it can’t be your memory.

THE HONEST PART

This role sits in an odd space for now: senior in scope and judgement, without a team underneath it yet. Until the People Partner joins later in 2027, you’ll also be the whole operational team, so a payroll deadline and a complex grievance can land in the same week. That eases as the function grows, but it means the authority you carry day to day has to come from the quality of your work, not a job title.

You are not designing the People strategy or the systems architecture. The CPO does that. What you get instead is real ownership of the hardest cases and the initiatives that matter, a close working relationship with the CPO, and a genuine path toward leading the People Partner practice as it grows.

You will set the direction for ExTrac's defence business: deciding which customers, programmes and markets we pursue, building the pipeline and partnerships to win them, and growing the team that delivers it. Defence growth strategy

Senior relationships and positioning

Customer insight into product

📈 Who We Are:

We are rebuilding the energy transaction, making it transparent and fair.

We're rebuilding how energy is bought and sold. That means cutting out middlemen, connecting businesses directly with renewable generators, and ensuring every transaction is traceable and transparent.

We're a 160+ person team - operators, data scientists, engineers, customer champions and energy experts - backed by top-tier investors including Lightspeed Venture Partners, Hitachi Ventures, Allianz, AlbionVC and Atomico. We closed a $75M Series B round in early 2026, taking our total funding to $94M, and we now power energy for over 4,000 UK businesses across 8,500+ sites, with over £75m in value returned to businesses and generators so far.

We're a technology company solving the energy industry, not an energy company. Some people call us a neo-utility, the neo-bank idea, applied to energy.

The industry is noticing. We were crowned Europe's Most Exciting Tech Company at the GP Bullhound Allstars awards, came in at #6 on LinkedIn's Top Startups 2026 in the UK, #7 on the Scaling Europe 50 of Europe's fastest-growing companies, and #14 on Sifted's AI 100.

Learn more about us on our website.

🚀 The Role

We're hiring a People Performance Manager to join our Performance Service.

tem is growing fast. Our goal is to get better as we get bigger - revenue growing faster than headcount. In practice that means keeping our strongest people engaged and performing, getting new joiners productive quickly, and enabling our leaders to multiply their impact over time. Most companies solve that with layers of management. We don't. Our leaders (Player-Coaches) coach their teams while staying hands-on with the work, which means the systems around them have to do more of the lifting. That's where the Performance Service comes in.

We're a team of four, and we own how tem runs as an organisation: the operating rhythm (how work gets planned, tracked, escalated and reported), the onboarding and development that build capability, the frameworks that define what good performance looks like and how people progress and get paid, and the operational backbone of contracts, benefits and payroll. We don't own recruitment. We're adding a second Performance Partner because we need more hands on deck - both partnering with our leaders day to day, and building the frameworks that support them.

Your patch is sustained performance - the part that runs continuously once someone is through the door. You'll carry a portfolio of leaders across our Engines and Services that you're accountable for, and you'll co-own the frameworks that sit underneath them alongside the rest of the team. You will not be handed a finished playbook to administer. You'll report into the Performance Service Manager. HR experience is welcome but not required - we're open to operators, people who've led teams, and the sort of person who ends up owning whatever the company needs next.

In your first 12 months, you might:

  • Become the first call for a portfolio of leaders on anything to do with their people - performance calls, team decisions and hard conversations.

  • Co-design how progression, performance standards, evaluation and reward actually work at tem, alongside the rest of the Performance team.

  • Handle live cases end to end - performance management, difficult conversations, exits and restructures.

  • Use AI and automation so the operational layer runs itself and your time goes on judgement, not process.

  • Turn recurring employee and manager pain points into better processes, tools, guidance or self-service, and measure whether they work.

🛠️ Responsibilities

  • Coach and challenge: be a leader's first call on anything to do with their people - a decision they want a second view on, coaching on how to handle a situation, or a read on employment law - and hold a position when you disagree with them.

  • Raise the bar: hold leaders to a high standard on performance, potential, pay and progression - help them make sharper calls, and hold consistency across your patch.

  • Handle live cases end to end: performance management, difficult conversations, exits and restructures.

  • Build to delight: shape how progression, performance standards, evaluation and reward actually work at tem, alongside the rest of the Performance team. We treat our people like top athletes, and our aim is to delight them at every step of their employee experience - the systems around them have to express that at every contact point.

  • Design for our shape, not the textbook: we index on outcomes and impact in everything - how progression works, how teams are structured, what leaders spend their time on. Most standard people frameworks assume a management hierarchy we don't have.

  • Automate the repeatable: use AI and automation so the operational layer runs itself and your time goes on judgement, not process.

  • Think in process, scalability and iteration: turn recurring employee and manager pain points into better processes, tools, guidance or self-service. Measure whether they work and redesign when they don't fit the purpose.

✅ Requirements

You do not need a CIPD qualification, and you do not need to have worked in a large, established HR function. You might have been a founder's associate or Chief of Staff at a Series A or B startup, holding the place together while it scaled. You might have built a People function from scratch and taken it from a one-person band to a well-oiled machine. You might have run a team or an Operations function where the people calls were effectively yours, even if People or HR never appeared in your job title. Or you might have done a different job that helped you build the skills below. A background in HR might help you do this job well, but it is not a requirement.

Must-Haves

  • You've held real accountability for decisions on people - you've partnered with leaders, or managed a team yourself, where hiring, performance and exit calls were either yours or made on your guidance.

  • You can be trusted with the hardest conversations in the business and you're recognised for how you handle them, and you understand how decisions about people shape culture and employer brand - balancing efficiency with empathy.

  • You've worked in or towards building a high-performance culture, and you're a confident challenger who carries conviction and can influence leadership decisions.

  • You're comfortable operating without a playbook, in a company where the requirements and the shape of your role change constantly.

  • You think from first principles, get to the root cause of complex problems, weigh competing considerations and anticipate second-order consequences.

  • You're fluent with Notion, automation and AI tooling - your instinct is to build the thing rather than do it manually a second time - and you write clearly enough that a busy person reads it once and comes away with a clear idea of the situation and the next actions.

Desirable

  • Employment relations experience in the UK, Europe or the US - we operate across the UK and Europe today, with plans to expand to the US soon.

  • Experience working across multiple countries, including employer of record arrangements.

  • Compensation and benchmarking experience - salary banding, pay review cycles, market data.

🎁 Benefits & Perks

  • Stock options so everyone has ownership in our mission.

  • 25 days holiday plus public holidays. Swap public holidays for the ones that matter most to you, and enjoy your birthday off.

  • Remote first and flexible working, with clear core hours and no internal meetings on Friday afternoons.

  • Up to GBP1,200 or EUR1,400 per year for your remote setup.

  • Up to GBP150 or EUR170 per month for wellbeing.

🤝 Interview Process

We move fast. Most processes take 2 to 3 weeks from first chat to offer. If you need us to adapt anything, let us know.

  • Intro call with our Talent team.

  • Skills interview, which might include a practical exercise we may ask you to prepare in advance.

We welcome applications from people of all backgrounds, experiences, and identities, including those that are traditionally underrepresented in the tech and energy sectors. Relay is fundamentally reshaping how goods move in an online era. Backed by Europe’s largest-ever logistics Series A ($35M) led by deep-tech investors Plural, and a recently closed Series B ($95M), Relay is scaling faster than 99% of venture-backed startups. We're assembling the most talent-dense team the logistics industry has ever seen

Relay’s Mission is to free commerce from friction. Today, high delivery costs act as a hidden tax on e-commerce, quietly shaping what can be sold online and limiting who can participate. We envision a world where more goods move more freely between more people, making the online shopping experience seamless and accessible to everyone.

THE TEAM
• ~160 people, around half in engineering, product and data
• 45+ advanced degrees across computer science, mathematics and operations research
• Thousands of data points captured, calculated, analysed and predicted for every single parcel we handle
• An intellectually vibrant culture of first‑principles thinking, tight feedback loops and relentless experimentation

The role

Every parcel through our sort centres is handled by an operative. At peak, we need to hire up to 600 of them a week.

As Operations Manager, Operative Acquisition you'll own operative supply across our sortation sites: enough suitable, trained, compliant and active operatives to fill every shift. You'll build the funnel, reporting and automation that make supply repeatable rather than manual, and keep it ahead of demand as volume rises.

Volumes rise sharply into November and December. Supply, not demand, will be the constraint. This role exists to make sure it isn't.

You'll be the single owner of the operative funnel, working across acquisition (including paid channels), Live Operations, our site teams, and Product and Engineering, who build the integrations the funnel runs on. You'll write SQL, ship automation, and spend time at our sort centres seeing how new starters actually land.

What you'll do

  • Own the operative funnel end to end, from applicant attraction through qualification, training, activation and retention

  • Keep applicant supply ahead of site demand, forecasting how many applicants, training places and sessions are needed and directing spend where gaps exist

  • Improve qualification and compliance, owning Right to Work/KYC and working with Product and Engineering to reduce drop-off and speed up the process

  • Optimise training capacity and waitlists, making sure sessions are filled and candidates stay engaged

  • Get new starters onto shift quickly, supporting activation, shift fill, communications and low-fill processes

  • Reduce cancellations, no-shows and inactivity, using the root causes to improve communications, processes and policies

  • Own operative communications and compliance processes, including waitlist messaging, suspensions, strikes and shift-booking comms

  • Build clear funnel reporting and alerts, tracking volumes, conversion, time to hire and drop-off by site to identify issues early

Who Will Thrive in this role?

  • A growth or operations background. You treat supply as a daily number and act the same day it slips

  • Confident in SQL (BigQuery or similar). You build dashboards from raw data, not static trackers

  • Experience running a high-volume hiring or onboarding funnel, ideally for a frontline workforce

  • A working understanding of Right to Work checks, enough to see how checks and re-checks affect the funnel and operative status. Legal owns the detail, but this can't be a blank

  • Clear writing. You can write processes, requirements and comms that other teams rely on

  • Experience using data to identify trends and improve outcomes”.

Desirable

  • Comfortable with paid acquisition, Google Ads or similar, enough to read performance and brief changes when a site runs short

  • Experience onboarding couriers or drivers at a carrier or delivery platform

  • Experience working with Product and Engineering on integrations or APIs

  • Experience with predictive or candidate-quality modelling

Our Firm

Asset Management Services (“AMS”) is the asset management practice of Agentis Capital Advisors, a global infrastructure advisory and investment platform. AMS manages more than 120 infrastructure assets representing over $35bn in enterprise value across renewables, public-private partnerships, digital and social infrastructure. We support our clients over the life of their assets through four service pillars:

  • Financial Model Management – We build, standardise, enhance and maintain the financial models behind our clients’ funds and portfolio companies

  • Financial Services Management – We run the accounting, budgeting, lender compliance and financial reporting for project companies

  • Operations Management – We oversee the day-to-day management of assets, including contract administration, performance monitoring, and board and stakeholder support

  • Fund Operations & Reporting – We maintain the fund-level valuation models, NAV and exit calculations, and leadership and LP reporting

AMS gives private markets and infrastructure investors one consistent, auditable and trusted view of their portfolios, delivered as a managed service. Our clients include leading infrastructure funds, pension funds, developers and project companies. Our guiding principles of excellence, client success, commitment, people and entrepreneurship set us apart.

The Opportunity

Private-markets managers and large asset owners run their portfolios on hundreds of inconsistent models, built by different advisors in different formats. Valuation, investor reporting and portfolio oversight are slow, manual and hard to audit. AMS solves this. We take over a client’s portfolio models, rebuild them to one standard on our technology-enabled platform, and deliver a live, fund-level view of the whole portfolio. We maintain and enhance it with our specialists on an ongoing basis.

We are looking for a Head of Sales, UK & Europe, based in London, to take this service to market and expand our client base. This is a hands-on, player-coach role, reporting to the Agentis Capital Managing Partners.

This role suits a commercially driven seller who has sold value-added services into funds (e.g., fund administration, back-office, data, valuation or portfolio-monitoring software and services), selling to CEOs, heads of asset management, CFOs, COOs and finance teams of private-markets managers.
